title: Scalar cochain evaluation from an ordinary unit square
statement: Let C,J,B,F,tau,sigma,alpha,hAlpha,A be scalar-system data [def-coef-semilinear-system-models; def-coef-semilinear-derived-calculus]. Fix an index n and an ordinary scalar-evaluation natural isomorphism rho at n satisfying the specified ordinary unit equation. For every cochain complex P of B-systems, evaluation of the system universal scalar cochain counit followed by the exact evaluation localization factor and the localized cochain map of rho equals the derived evaluation comparison followed by finite scalar extension of the evaluation localization factor and the finite universal scalar cochain counit. This is a conditional compatibility result for a given rho, not an existence statement for rho.

source.place: sites-modules.tex, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules (03D7); sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-derived-base-change (06YY) and lemma-adjoint (07A6); step 2 of stage3-pur-extension-strict-derived-comparison.

proof.text: For each scalar datum form the derived cochain unit and the localization of the ordinary cochain unit as natural transformations out of Q. On K-flat complexes they agree by transpose_model at the identity. Resolve an arbitrary source by a K-flat complex, use naturality and cancel its localized augmentation, obtaining the cochain unit equation on every complex.

The exact functor composition and natural-isomorphism localization equations identify the derived restriction evaluation square with the localized ordinary cochain square. The hypothesis on rho gives the ordinary unit square degree by degree, hence after localization. Apply the supplied derived transpose_evaluation and the two cochain unit equations. Both counit composites have equal adjoints under the finite derived adjunction, so its Hom bijection proves their equality.

proof_origin.place: sites-modules.tex, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules (03D7); sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-derived-base-change (06YY) and lemma-adjoint (07A6). Ordinary comparison uses the proved sequence-site mate theorem; normalized units descend from K-flat source resolutions.

theorem scalarCochainEvaluation_of_unit (n : ℕ)
    (ρ : A.scalar.model.E ⋙ SemilinearSections.evaluation J F σ n ≅
      SemilinearSections.evaluation J B τ n ⋙ (A.levels n).model.E)
    (hρ : ∀ M,
      (SemilinearSections.evaluation J B τ n).map
          (A.scalar.ordinaryAdjunction.unit.app M) ≫
        (SemilinearSections.restrictionEvaluation_existsUnique
          J B τ F σ α hα n).exists.choose.hom.app (A.scalar.model.E.obj M) ≫
        (SemilinearSections.res (α n)).map (ρ.hom.app M) =
      (A.levels n).ordinaryAdjunction.unit.app
        ((SemilinearSections.evaluation J B τ n).obj M))
    (P : CochainComplex (SemilinearSections.Systems J B τ) ℤ) :
    (SemilinearSections.e J F σ n).map (A.scalar.model.ε.app P) ≫
        (SemilinearSections.evaluation J F σ n).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
          ((A.scalar.model.E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map ((NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex ρ (.up ℤ)).hom.app P) =
      (A.evaluation n).hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ≫
        (A.levels n).T.map
          ((SemilinearSections.evaluation J B τ n).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app P) ≫
        (A.levels n).model.ε.app
          (((SemilinearSections.evaluation J B τ n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)
